# Benchmarking and Improving Text-to-SQL Generation under Ambiguity

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#ambiqt)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.436.pdf) · EMNLP 2023 proceedings, printed pages 7053–7074

**Reading coverage:** All 22 pages: sections 1–7, limitations/ethics, algorithm 1, all result and ablation tables, and appendices A–F including prompts and SQL-output examples.

## Research question

A top-k SQL generator often returns superficial variants of one interpretation instead of covering plausible alternatives.

## Method

AmbiQT perturbs Spider schemas to construct two references per question across column, table, join and precomputed-aggregate ambiguity. LogicalBeam first generates plans/templates with controlled join/selection-count changes, then restricts infilling branches to schema names; candidates are combined with ordinary beam outputs.

## Evaluation

BothInTopK and EitherInTopK measure reference coverage among five outputs using execution matching, with exact-set-match results in the appendix. Historical T5, Flan-T5, RESDSQL, ChatGPT and Codex baselines are compared; standard Spider and KaggleDBQA top-five accuracy is also assessed.

## What the results support

Explicit structural and schema diversity increases coverage of both references. Ablations show different contributions by ambiguity type, and unrestricted sampling frequently repeats the same interpretation. The strongest relative gains depend on the chosen baseline and ambiguity category.

## Limits and qualifications

The English-only benchmark is built by controlled schema changes, not observed user interactions. Two references and four transformation families bound coverage; neither user clarification success nor all naturally possible interpretations is measured. Two decoding stages add work and residual alias variants remain.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A foundational interpretation-coverage benchmark and decoding baseline; top-five oracle coverage must remain separate from selecting the user-intended answer.
